notes: High overlap (Jaccard=0.8) on claims about multimodality debate and Marr-Albus theory (C7, C8, C84, C147). Both LLM and peer reviewers agree these core findings are strongly supported and unambiguously demonstrate granule cell multimodality.

Strong overlap (Jaccard=0.643) on M1-BPN connectivity and corollary discharge claims (C43, C74-C80, C83). Both agree evidence is insufficient: LLM notes lack of functional validation for corollary discharge identity; peer reviewers request quantitation and reproducibility data.

Moderate overlap (Jaccard=0.467) on ECN-BPN convergence onto granule cells (C5, C41, C55, C56, C81, C84, C101). Both agree the anatomical evidence at synaptic resolution strongly supports multimodal granule cells. Peer review includes additional regional mapping claims (C6, C42, C82, C102) also rated SUPPORTED.

Low overlap (Jaccard=0.154) but shared claims on regional mapping (C6, C42, C82, C102). Both agree the spatial distribution patterns across cerebellar cortex are well-supported. LLM R2 focuses exclusively on regional organization while peer R1 combines this with convergence evidence.

Low overlap (Jaccard=0.222) on coordinate transformation and forward model claims (C128, C133-C135). LLM rates as UNSUPPORTED (explicitly speculative, no functional validation); peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN (not persuasive but request discussion rather than rejection). Disagreement reflects different thresholds for speculation vs. unsupported claims.

Low overlap (Jaccard=0.238) with shared claims on corollary discharge and internal models (C9, C83, C125, C130-C131). Both rate UNCERTAIN but focus on different aspects: LLM emphasizes lack of functional validation for corollary discharge; peer reviewers question theoretical interpretation of convergence for learning mechanisms.

LLM-only evaluation of methodological limitations and conservative interpretation (C105-C107). No corresponding peer review result addresses these specific claims about underestimation of multimodality prevalence.
